title: Analysis for Non-Majors
description: The Mathematics Department's real analysis course for non-majors: the real numbers, bounds and completeness, sequences and their convergence, series, limits and continuity, differentiability and the mean value theorems, Taylor's theorem and L'Hopital's rule, and the Riemann integral. Built from the MAT 223 lecture notes in the course folder (scanned) and its past papers from 2008/09 to 2020/21.

topics.title: The Real Numbers: Bounds, Supremum and Completeness
topics.summary: The real numbers form a complete ordered field. A set is bounded above or below if some real number bounds it; its least upper bound is the supremum and its greatest lower bound the infimum. The rationals are dense but not complete: there is no rational x with x^2 = 2.
subtopics: Completeness and the irrationality of the square root of 2

topics.title: Sequences of Real Numbers
topics.summary: A sequence converges to a if for every ε > 0 there is n(ε) such that |a_n − a| < ε for all n ≥ n(ε). Limits are unique, convergent sequences are bounded, but boundedness alone does not guarantee convergence. Bounded monotone sequences converge, and a Cauchy sequence is one whose terms get arbitrarily close to each other.
subtopics: Proving limits with ε and n(ε)

topics.title: Series of Real Numbers
topics.summary: A series is the sequence of its partial sums S_n = a_1 + ... + a_n; it converges to a if S_n converges to a. Geometric series with ratio |r| < 1 converge to a/(1 − r). Tests for convergence include the nth-term test, comparison, the ratio test and absolute convergence.

topics.title: Limits and Continuity of Functions
topics.summary: A function of a real variable assigns one value to each point of its domain. A function is continuous at x0 if for every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with |f(x) − f(x0)| < ε whenever |x − x0| < δ, equivalently if f(x_n) → f(x0) for every sequence x_n → x0. Sums, products and compositions of continuous functions are continuous, and continuity on a closed bounded interval gives uniform continuity.
subtopics: Algebra of continuous functions and uniform continuity

topics.title: Differentiability and the Mean Value Theorems
topics.summary: The derivative f'(x0) is the limit of the difference quotient (f(x) − f(x0))/(x − x0), the slope of the tangent. Differentiability implies continuity but not conversely. Rolle's theorem, the mean value theorem, Fermat's theorem and Darboux's theorem describe derivatives and locate critical points, maxima and minima.
subtopics: The difference quotient and the derivative

topics.title: Taylor's Theorem and L'Hopital's Rule
topics.summary: Higher derivatives are defined inductively. Taylor's theorem approximates a function near a point by a polynomial in its derivatives, with a remainder, and gives estimates such as the square root of 1.2. L'Hopital's rule, derived from the Cauchy mean value theorem, evaluates limits of indeterminate forms 0/0 and ∞/∞.

topics.title: The Riemann Integral
topics.summary: A partition of [a, b] divides it into subintervals; upper and lower sums U(f, P) and L(f, P) bound the area. Refinements increase L and decrease U. f is Riemann integrable when the upper and lower integrals agree, tested by the Darboux criterion or the limit criterion with regular partitions. Continuous and monotone functions are integrable, and the inequality and triangle rules bound integrals.
subtopics: The limit test with regular partitions
Properties: inequality rule, triangle rule and integral functions
